target_customer: Businesses with surplus food and inventory such as cafeterias, universities, hospitals, grocers and caterers
problem: Surplus edible food is thrown away while nonprofits need it; the gap is logistics, not scarcity.
business_model: B2B software and logistics subscription plus pay-as-you-go; nonprofits join free
product_category: Food waste and surplus redistribution platform

founders.name: Komal Ahmad
education: UC Berkeley (student when she started, per sources seen in search)
previous_startups: Feeding Forward (earlier name of the same company)
founders.background_notes: YC page bio lists Forbes 30 Under 30 and other honors; it does not give prior employers.

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and dispatch app with logistics, tax and impact reporting is standard software; the hard part is operations and driver coordination.

defensibility.rationale: A two sided network of donors and nonprofits helps, but competing food rescue nonprofits and apps existed and the model depends on local logistics.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy by a large player found.

market_need_then: Founder statement quoted in sources: hunger is a logistics problem, not a scarcity problem. Her story of a veteran at a Berkeley campus food recovery effort is told in sources seen only in snippets. No dated spend data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission and impact framed with for-profit positioning

branding.brand_signature: Founder story and awards (Forbes 30 Under 30, Nelson Mandela Humanitarian Award per YC bio)
branding.community_and_virality: Featured by Business Insider and Fast Company according to logos on its site.

brand_strength.rationale: Founder profile drives press, but the name collides with Copia Automation, Copia Global and a Kenyan retailer called Copia, which pollutes search results.

outcome_analysis: Copia, previously Feeding Forward, is still operating and sells an enterprise redistribution engine with customers such as Cheesecake Factory and Sutter Health. Its reported impact figures are large but company stated, and no funding round could be verified, so growth quality is unclear. Search results about layoffs and shutdown concern Kenya's unrelated Copia.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators give a 3M seed in March 2016, a 1M seed in 2019, and CB Insights 280K over four rounds; VCBacked lists 150K. These conflict and come from aggregators, so no round is recorded. The Waste360 article and Wikipedia-style competitor sources returned 403 and are not used; Replate (founded 2016) and Food Rescue US appear in an undated search snippet, so competitor list left empty. Some directories name Kimberly Smith as CEO; the YC page names Komal Ahmad. Education claim for Ahmad comes from search summaries, not a page opened.
